We stress that Lemma 12 solves these three instances exactly, not merely up to rounding: an independent exhaustive solution of the integer programme max{∑h:∑h2=n⋅2n−1,h≡n(2),|h|≤n}\max\{\sum h:\sum h^{2}=n\cdot 2^{n-1},\ h\equiv n\ (2),\ |h|\leq n\} by dynamic programming over the sum-of-squares budget (the displayed |h|≤n|h|\leq n is automatic for any realisable local field because h=2​degE​(v)−nh=2\deg_{E}(v)-n; it is included only to make the finite computational state space explicit and is not used in the closed-form upper-bound proof) returns optima 7272, 160160, 340340 for n=6,7,8n=6,7,8 respectively, matching the bounds above, and returns exactly 33, 11 and 22 optimal hh-distributions respectively — for n=6n=6, {2:30,6:2}\{2{:}30,6{:}2\}, {0:1,2:27,4:3,6:1}\{0{:}1,2{:}27,4{:}3,6{:}1\} and {0:2,2:24,4:6}\{0{:}2,2{:}24,4{:}6\} (labelled A, B and C throughout; in DPTV79’s Table I terms, C is their “first solution” and A and B are their “other solutions”, the realisable one thus being C, see Section 6.3); for n=7n=7, {1:16,3:48}\{1{:}16,3{:}48\}; for n=8n=8, {2:87,4:40,6:1}\{2{:}87,4{:}40,6{:}1\} and {0:1,2:84,4:43}\{0{:}1,2{:}84,4{:}43\}. These counts also follow from Lemma 12 in a line, so the enumeration is a check and not a source. The multiplicity phenomenon itself is independently citable: DPTV79 record (p. 621) that when the optimum concentrates on three or four integers they find many solutions, and that this happens exactly at d=6d=6 and d=8d=8 – the two dimensions at which the programme here returns more than one optimal distribution. At n=7n=7, Δ=0\Delta=0 forces h∈{1,3}h\in\{1,3\} pointwise and ∑h=160\sum h=160 over |U|=64|U|=64 then fixes the multiplicities, giving one distribution. At n=6n=6, the Δ=16\Delta=16 analysis above already fixes exactly two vertices at h∈{0,6}h\in\{0,6\} and the other 3030 at h∈{2,4}h\in\{2,4\}; writing jj for the number of those two at h=6h=6 and kk for the number of the remaining 3030 at h=4h=4, ∑h=72\sum h=72 reads 6​j+4​k+2​(30−k)=726j+4k+2(30-k)=72, i.e. 3​j+k=63j+k=6, whose solutions (j,k)=(2,0),(1,3),(0,6)(j,k)=(2,0),(1,3),(0,6) give exactly A, B and C. At n=8n=8, the Δ=8\Delta=8 analysis above leaves one vertex at h∈{0,6}h\in\{0,6\} and 127127 at h∈{2,4}h\in\{2,4\}; the same count gives 3​j+k=433j+k=43 with j∈{0,1}j\in\{0,1\}, hence (j,k)=(1,40)(j,k)=(1,40) and (0,43)(0,43) — the two distributions above. Whether some odd-square 682682-edge set realises {2:87,4:40,6:1}\{2{:}87,4{:}40,6{:}1\} on both sides we have not determined. For n=7n=7, the unique optimal distribution is necessarily realised. Thus n=8n=8 is qualitatively different from n=6n=6: all optimal field distributions for n=8n=8 admit a realisation, while for n=6n=6 only one does. In each case computation is reproducible with the bundled solve_field_ip.py (standard library only, seconds to run); it is a check on the closed-form argument above, not a substitute for it, and the two are logically independent in a sense worth making explicit: the upper bound S≤72,160,340S\leq 72,160,340 is established by Lemma 12 together with nonnegativity, integrality and the parity of SS (the congruence adding essential strength only at n=6n=6), without reference to how many configurations attain it – the argument in each of the three cases above shows directly that no integer solution exceeds the stated value, full stop. The DP’s role is only to confirm, separately, that the count of optimal hh-distributions (as opposed to spin configurations realising them) is exactly 3,1,23,1,2 – and this too is a complete count, not a sample. To be precise, the code groups equal field values and enumerates count distributions {h:multiplicity}\{h{:}\text{multiplicity}\}, not the exponentially many ordered assignments of hh-values to vertices; within this count-distribution state space, both the optimisation pass (forward DP) and the enumeration pass (backtracking reconstruction) traverse the same (i,k,s)(i,k,s) state tree exhaustively, so completeness of the list follows from the same recursion that establishes correctness of the optimum, rather than from a separate argument.

All three upper bounds g⁡(6)≤132g(6)\leq 132, g⁡(7)≤304g(7)\leq 304 and g⁡(8)≤682g(8)\leq 682 are thus established directly from Lemma 9 and Lemma 12 – reproducing, by a closed-form argument that makes the reasoning self-contained, the n=6,7,8n=6,7,8 entries among the optima DPTV79’s Table I tabulates for n≤10n\leq 10, and supplying a public machine-verifiable certificate at n=8n=8 after DPTV79 left that dimension open and MPR95 later reported attainment without releasing a configuration (Section 6.3); we retain the citations to Derrida et al. [5] and Marinari–Parisi–Ritort [15] for historical priority and for the connection that prompted this section, not because the upper-bound proof depends on them.

Marinari, Parisi, and Ritort [15] report having exhibited, by simulated annealing, a D=8D=8 ground state attaining Derrida et al.’s improved energy lower bound. Their attainment claim, under the correspondence developed below, corresponds to the same bound value ∑v∈Uh⁡(v)=340\sum_{v\in U}h(v)=340 established directly above – MPR95 do not themselves report a quantity called SS or 340340; the correspondence is ours. Their Hamiltonian is H≡−D−1/2∑(x,y)Jx,ysxsyH\equiv-D^{-1/2}\sum_{(x,y)}J_{x,y}s_{x}s_{y} [15, Eq. 3]; writing S=∑(x,y)Jx,y​sx​syS=\sum_{(x,y)}J_{x,y}s_{x}s_{y} for the sum over all edges (not just UU), a bipartite argument identical to the one used for Lemma 9 shows S=∑v∈Uh⁡(v)S=\sum_{v\in U}h(v) exactly (every edge has exactly one endpoint in UU, so summing the local field over UU counts each edge’s sign once), so H=−S/DH=-S/\sqrt{D} and, per site, H/N=−S/(ND)H/N=-S/(N\sqrt{D}) with N=2DN=2^{D}. Since each positive edge contributes +1+1 to SS and each negative edge contributes −1-1, S=|E|−(D​2D−1−|E|)=2​|E|−D​2D−1S=|E|-(D2^{D-1}-|E|)=2|E|-D2^{D-1}, hence explicitly

|E|=D​2D−1−N​D​(H/N)2.|E|=\frac{D2^{D-1}-N\sqrt{D}\,(H/N)}{2}.

At D=8,S=340D=8,S=340 (equivalently |E|=(1024+340)/2=682|E|=(1024+340)/2=682) this is, step by step, H/N=−S/(ND)=−340/(2568)=−340/724.077…=−0.46956…H/N=-S/(N\sqrt{D})=-340/(256\sqrt{8})=-340/724.077\ldots=-0.46956\ldots, i.e. H≈−120.2H\approx-120.2, about −0.470-0.470 per site. As a cross-check against MPR95’s own text: they report (in their D=9D{=}9 discussion, pp. 3–4 of arXiv:cond-mat/9410089, the passage checked at page level as recorded in the Acknowledgements) that “on a scale where the minimal energy jump is 1” their D=9 naive bound H/N=−1/2H/N=-1/2 corresponds to an integer value of −384-384 (i.e. a scale factor of 768=384/(1/2)768=384/(1/2)), and state that on this same scale “the improved lower bound at D=8D=8 gives −361-361” – note this 768768 factor is MPR95’s own D=9D{=}9 comparison scale, not an intrinsic D=8D{=}8 energy-quantisation unit; they use it purely to compare bound values across dimensions on one common integer axis. Applying the same factor (as MPR95 themselves do for the D=8D=8 figure) to our value gives 768×(−0.4696​…)=−360.62​…≈−361768\times(-0.4696\ldots)=-360.62\ldots\approx-361, matching their reported integer to within rounding. In one line, the affine correspondence is

−361=round⁡(768⋅−S28​8)at ​S=340,|E|=1024+S2=682.-361=\operatorname{round}\!\Bigl(768\cdot\frac{-S}{2^{8}\sqrt{8}}\Bigr)\quad\text{at }S=340,\qquad|E|=\frac{1024+S}{2}=682.

The identification is not an accident of the rounding width: the nearest admissible value below, S=338S=338, gives −359-359 under the same nearest-integer rounding rule, and S=336S=336 gives −356-356, so among the admissible values (even S≤341⁤13S\leq 341\tfrac{1}{3}, of which 340340 is the largest) only S=340S=340 rounds to −361-361; the identification even survives one step past the bound, since the inadmissible S=342S=342 and S=344S=344 (both excluded by nonnegativity) would give −363-363 and −365-365. Three further data points fix and test the scale under the identical rule; their evidentiary roles differ, so we state them once here to keep the count straight: the D=9D=9 bound value calibrates the scale (it is what pins 768768 down, so it is not an independent check); the D=8D=8 and D=10D=10 values are the two independent checks; and the D=9D=9 attained value is a bound-free corroboration at the calibration dimension. First the calibration point: at D=9D=9, 9=3\sqrt{9}=3 is itself an integer of the right parity, so the field-bound optimum is the unique uniform distribution h≡3h\equiv 3, giving S=768S=768, H/N=−1/2H/N=-1/2 exactly, and 768×(−1/2)=−384768\times(-1/2)=-384 – an exact match to the value MPR95 state at D=9D=9. That value is the field-bound target, not an attained ground state: MPR95 report failing to reach it, obtaining −0.494792-0.494792, i.e. −380-380 on the same scale, four units short. Whether the bound is attained at n=9n=9 is open here too (Open Problem 7). The agreement to be read off this point is therefore between two computations of the same bound, not evidence about g⁡(9)g(9). This point, however, is where the scale factor 768768 is itself pinned down, so it corroborates the conversion without being independent of it; the two independent checks are D=8D=8 and D=10D=10. At D=10D=10, m=512m=512, Q=5120Q=5120, (a,b)=(2,4)(a,b)=(2,4) gives Δ=9216−6​S\Delta=9216-6S, so S≤1536S\leq 1536 (with Δ=0\Delta=0, distribution {2:256,4:256}\{2{:}256,4{:}256\}), and 768×(−1536/(102410))≈−364.29≈−364768\times(-1536/(1024\sqrt{10}))\approx-364.29\approx-364, matching MPR95’s reported D=10D=10 value of −364-364 to the same rounding rule. The scale factor is in fact forced rather than fitted. Every configuration has S=2​|E|−D​ 2D−1S=2|E|-D\,2^{D-1} with D​ 2D−1D\,2^{D-1} even for D≥2D\geq 2, so SS is an even integer and the achievable values of H/N=−S/(ND)H/N=-S/(N\sqrt{D}) lie on a lattice of pitch 2/(N​D)2/(N\sqrt{D}). (A single spin flip at vv changes SS by −2​h​(v)-2h(v) and hence H/NH/N by 2​|h⁡(v)|/(N​D)2|h(v)|/(N\sqrt{D}) in magnitude – a vertex-dependent multiple of the pitch, equal to the pitch itself only when |h⁡(v)|=1|h(v)|=1; for even DD every h⁡(v)h(v) is even, so no single flip ever realises the pitch there. The quantisation unit is the lattice pitch, not any particular flip.) At D=9D=9 the pitch is 2/(512⋅3)=1/7682/(512\cdot 3)=1/768, so 768768 is what MPR95’s “minimum energy jump equal to 11” scale must mean there; the same pitch at D=8D=8 is 2/(256⋅2​2)=1/(256​2)≈1/362.042/(256\cdot 2\sqrt{2})=1/(256\sqrt{2})\approx 1/362.04, confirming that 768768 is not a D=8D=8 quantisation unit. A further point corroborates it empirically: MPR95 also report their attained D=9D=9 value both as −0.494792-0.494792 and as −380-380 on the integer scale, and 768×(−0.494792)=−379.99​…768\times(-0.494792)=-379.99\ldots, so 768768 is forced by a datum that involves no bound at all; being a D=9D=9 datum it shares the calibration dimension, so we count it as corroboration rather than as a third independent check. The obvious rival reading — one unit per minimal energy jump in each dimension — is excluded: it reproduces −384-384 at D=9D=9 but gives −S/2=−170-S/2=-170 at D=8D=8, nowhere near MPR95’s −361-361. All four data points – the calibrating D=9D=9 bound, the two independent checks at D=8D=8 and D=10D=10, and the bound-free D=9D=9 attained value – agree under one scale, which is considerably stronger than the D=8D=8 figure alone. Their paper reports the D=8D=8 attainment in energy units only, without an explicit spin configuration or its translation into edge-count terms; we supply that translation and an explicit, machine-verified 682682-edge certificate in Section 6.3 below. Under the correspondence of Section 6, this historical attainment report at D=8D=8 corresponds to g⁡(8)=682g(8)=682, matching what was already established above from Lemma 9 together with the integer/parity constraints and elementary inequalities alone (as detailed above, Lemma 11 is not needed for this bound); the explicit witness realising it is due to the present reconstruction, prompted by S. Lai’s identification of the connection to [5, 15]. Together with the matching witnesses at n=6,7n=6,7 this gives Theorem 1: g⁡(6)=132g(6)=132, g⁡(7)=304g(7)=304, and g⁡(8)=682g(8)=682, each half of each equality now carried by material released with this paper.

6.3 Verification

We constructed explicit witnesses for all three values and machine-verified them independently of [5, 15, 11].

Q6Q_{6}, g⁡(6)=132g(6)=132. We obtained a 132-edge odd-square witness for Q6Q_{6} by the same route used for Q8Q_{8} below: the canonical fully frustrated coupling

J⁡(x,dim)=(−1)popcount⁡(x&(2dim−1)),J(x,\mathrm{dim})=(-1)^{\mathrm{popcount}(x\,\&\,(2^{\mathrm{dim}}-1))},

verified fully frustrated on Q6Q_{6} (all 240240 squares have coupling product −1-1, no exceptions), together with a 6464-bit spin configuration. Because switching preserves frustration, the set of edges on which J⁡(x,y)​sx​sy=+1J(x,y)s_{x}s_{y}=+1 is odd-square for every spin assignment, so the construction reduces to maximising that edge count, i.e. to a ground-state search. We ran a fixed-seed simulated annealing over the 6464 spins (search_q6.py, seed 2026082320260823), which reached 132132 edges on its first trial; the run is exactly reproducible from the released script. The resulting witness is regenerated and self-checked by generate_q6_132.py and released as q6_odd_square_132.json.

Proposition 13.

The Q6Q_{6} witness edge set satisfies:

More precisely, adding any of the 6060 non-edges creates at least two new C4C_{4}s; the distribution of the number of newly completed C4C_{4}s per non-edge is {2:2,3:29,4:26,5:3}\{2{:}2,3{:}29,4{:}26,5{:}3\}.

The distribution in (iv) is one of the exactly three optimal hh-distributions enumerated in Section 6.2, so the witness attains the upper bound S≤72S\leq 72 there and settles g⁡(6)=132g(6)=132. Two further remarks. First, it coincides in multiplicities with the local-field distribution Derrida et al. report for their D=6D=6 configuration, “n⁡(4)=6n(4)=6; n⁡(2)=24n(2)=24; n⁡(0)=2n(0)=2” [5, p. 622]; we did not reconstruct their configuration and do not claim the two edge sets agree, only that our independently found witness realises the same distribution. DPTV79 also report 3030 overfrustrated plaquettes out of 240240 for their H6H_{6} configuration, matching the 3030 squares in the 11-edge class of our histogram {1:30,3:210}\{1{:}30,3{:}210\} under the complementary positive-edge convention; this is a further consistency check, though a forced one: with 132132 positive edges the double count of Proposition 13(ii) already fixes N1=30N_{1}=30, so this agrees with DPTV rather than confirming anything independent, not an edge-set identity claim. Second, this witness is not the released 132-edge Q6Q_{6} construction q6_edges_132.jsonl of Section 9: their symmetric difference has size |E​△​E′|=62|E\triangle E^{\prime}|=62, and the latter is C4C_{4}-free but not odd-square (square-intersection histogram {:8,:44,:188}\{1\!:\!8,\,2\!:\!44,\,3\!:\!188\}, and ∑v∈Uh​(v)2=176≠192\sum_{v\in U}h(v)^{2}=176\neq 192). Both are 132132-edge C4C_{4}-free subgraphs of Q6Q_{6}; only the new one is a witness for g⁡(6)g(6) specifically.

Realizability of the other two optimal n=6n=6 field distributions: an exhaustive decision. The field-bound DP (Section 6.2; solve_field_ip.py) identifies exactly three optimal hh-distributions on UU for n=6n=6, labelled as there: distribution C ={0:2,2:24,4:6}=\{0{:}2,2{:}24,4{:}6\} (realised above), A ={2:30,6:2}=\{2{:}30,6{:}2\}, and B ={0:1,2:27,4:3,6:1}=\{0{:}1,2{:}27,4{:}3,6{:}1\}. DPTV79 (p. 622) noted that solutions besides their first were listed in Table I and asked whether any is realisable (“We do not know if the other solutions … are realizable”, in the plural; we rely on that sentence for the existence of at least two further solutions, not on a reading of the typeset table itself, which we could not extract). Since DPTV’s constraints are the ones solved here and the exhaustive enumeration returns exactly three optimal distributions, their “other solutions” are necessarily A and B; the identification is forced by the completeness of the enumeration rather than by transcription of the table. To be explicit about the evidence: we have read DPTV79 pp. 620–622 directly, but Table I itself does not extract as text from the journal PDF and we have not transcribed it, so every statement here about its contents rests on DPTV’s surrounding prose together with our own enumeration. MPR95 reported, by simulated annealing, that at D=6D=6 only configurations corresponding to the first solution of DPTV’s Table I are realisable and that “the other solution of the Diophantine equation seems not to correspond to any spin configuration” – a tentative negative finding, in the singular, with no released configuration or decision procedure. (Note the grammatical mismatch between the two sources themselves: DPTV79 write “the other solutions” where MPR95 write “the other solution”; on the exhaustive count below – exactly three optima, of which two are non-realisable – the plural is the accurate reading, and we take MPR95’s singular as loose phrasing rather than as a competing count.) Since Proposition 13 identifies C with DPTV’s first solution by multiplicity, the question is whether A and B are realisable. Here “realisable” prescribes the histogram on the chosen bipartition side UU only; UcU^{c} is not constrained. This is the same one-side convention used by DPTV79 for n⁡(h)n(h). Each of A, B, and C has S=72S=72, so any realisable target automatically has |E|=(192+72)/2=132|E|=(192+72)/2=132. We settle the one-side decision exhaustively rather than heuristically.

Proposition 14 (Exhaustive decision).

Among 132132-edge odd-square subgraphs of Q6Q_{6}, distribution C is realised as the local-field histogram on UU – throughout this proposition the histogram is prescribed on the fixed bipartition side UU only, with UcU^{c} unconstrained, the same one-side convention as DPTV79’s n⁡(h)n(h) – and distributions A and B are not realised on UU by any such subgraph. (By the translation symmetry noted in the proof the restriction to UU costs nothing: g⁡(n)g(n) itself is two-side symmetric, and a distribution realised on one side is realised on the other.)

Proof.

By Lemma 8 the odd-square edge sets of Q6Q_{6} are exactly the positive-edge sets arising from spin configurations under any fixed fully frustrated coupling, so it suffices to decide the question for the canonical coupling used throughout; the conclusion is independent of that choice. Write sv=(−1)tvs_{v}=(-1)^{t_{v}} with tv∈{0,1}t_{v}\in\{0,1\}, and let b⁡(v,w)=1b(v,w)=1 exactly when J⁡(v,w)=−1J(v,w)=-1; an edge v​wvw is positive iff tv⊕tw=b⁡(v,w)t_{v}\oplus t_{w}=b(v,w). As Q6Q_{6} is bipartite, every neighbour of v∈Uv\in U lies in UcU^{c}, so

k⁡(v)=#⁡{i:tv⊕ei⊕b⁡(v,i)=1}k(v)\;=\;\#\{\,i:\;t_{v\oplus e_{i}}\oplus b(v,i)=1\,\}

depends only on the 3232 spins on UcU^{c}, and deg⁡(v)=k⁡(v)\deg(v)=k(v) if tv=1t_{v}=1, deg⁡(v)=6−k⁡(v)\deg(v)=6-k(v) if tv=0t_{v}=0. Hence each tvt_{v} (v∈Uv\in U) is a free independent choice, and the achievable degree at vv is exactly one of k⁡(v)k(v), 6−k⁡(v)6-k(v). With h=2​deg−6h=2\deg-6, the achievable nonnegative field is h=6−2​m​(v)h=6-2m(v) where m⁡(v)=min⁡(k⁡(v),6−k⁡(v))∈{0,1,2,3}m(v)=\min(k(v),6-k(v))\in\{0,1,2,3\}, so m=0,1,2,3m=0,1,2,3 correspond to h=6,4,2,0h=6,4,2,0 respectively. A target hh-histogram on UU is therefore realisable if and only if the multiset {m⁡(v):v∈U}\{m(v):v\in U\} equals the induced mm-multiset for some assignment of the 3232 spins on UcU^{c}. (This step uses that the target histogram has no negative entry, so that the achievable field at each vv is the single value 6−2​m​(v)6-2m(v); A, B and C are all nonnegative, and by the remark after Lemma 9 no optimal distribution can have one. It also suffices to decide the question on UU: translation by e0e_{0} is an automorphism of Q6Q_{6} exchanging UU and UcU^{c}, and it carries edge sets to edge sets preserving both size and odd-squareness, so a distribution realised on one side is realised on the other.) The mm-multisets are {0:2,2:30}\{0{:}2,2{:}30\} for A, {0:1,1:3,2:27,3:1}\{0{:}1,1{:}3,2{:}27,3{:}1\} for B, and {1:6,2:24,3:2}\{1{:}6,2{:}24,3{:}2\} for C. This is a finite (2322^{32}) decision problem. For A and B it is settled without any search at all, by a parity obstruction. Since deg⁡(v)\deg(v) is k⁡(v)k(v) or 6−k⁡(v)6-k(v), we have k⁡(v)=(h⁡(v)+6)/2k(v)=(h(v)+6)/2 or (6−h⁡(v))/2(6-h(v))/2; these differ by h⁡(v)h(v), which is even, so the parity of k⁡(v)k(v) is determined by h⁡(v)h(v) alone, independently of the free spin tvt_{v}:

k⁡(v)≡h⁡(v)+62(mod2),i.e.k⁡(v)​ odd⇔h⁡(v)∈{0,4}.k(v)\equiv\tfrac{h(v)+6}{2}\pmod{2},\qquad\text{i.e.}\qquad k(v)\text{ odd}\iff h(v)\in\{0,4\}.

(Explicitly over the even range: h=0,2,4,6h=0,2,4,6 give h+62=3,4,5,6\tfrac{h+6}{2}=3,4,5,6, of which 33 and 55 are odd.) Reducing the definition of k⁡(v)k(v) modulo 22 gives k⁡(v)≡∑itv⊕ei+∑ib⁡(v,i)k(v)\equiv\sum_{i}t_{v\oplus e_{i}}+\sum_{i}b(v,i), so the parity vector p∈GF​(2)Up\in\mathrm{GF}(2)^{U} is the affine image p=M​t+Bp=Mt+B, where MM is the U×UcU\times U^{c} bipartite incidence matrix of Q6Q_{6} over GF⁡(2)\mathrm{GF}(2) and B⁡(v)=∑ib⁡(v,i)B(v)=\sum_{i}b(v,i). The reachable parity vectors are exactly the coset B+Im⁡(M)B+\operatorname{Im}(M). Here MM has rank 1616, and that coset — 2162^{16} vectors — has weight distribution

{8:640, 12:13824, 16:36608, 20:13824, 24:640},\{8{:}640,\;12{:}13824,\;16{:}36608,\;20{:}13824,\;24{:}640\},

so every reachable parity vector has weight in {8,12,16,20,24}\{8,12,16,20,24\}. A target histogram fixes that weight: it is the number of its vertices with h∈{0,4}h\in\{0,4\}, namely 00 for A and 1+3=41+3=4 for B. Neither occurs, so A and B are not realisable — and this needs no enumeration of mm-multisets. Distribution C requires weight 2+6=82+6=8, which does occur, and the witness of Section 6.3 realises it. For completeness we also settled all three by depth-first search with counter-overflow pruning, which agrees (the node counts below are properties of this implementation and its search order, recorded for orientation only: they carry no reproduction obligation, and a differently ordered search will visit different counts; the parity obstruction above is the search-order-independent proof): the search assigns the 3232 UcU^{c} spins in a fixed index order and keeps one running counter per value m∈{0,1,2,3}m\in\{0,1,2,3\}; a v∈Uv\in U has m⁡(v)m(v) determined as soon as the last of its six neighbours in that order is assigned, at which point m⁡(v)m(v) is tallied, and the branch is cut the moment any counter exceeds the target’s multiplicity for that value. Global spin flip fixes every hh, so the first UcU^{c} spin may be pinned without loss of generality (each sign configuration has exactly one lift with the pinned value). The search finds a realisation for C (501501 nodes visited) and exhausts the space for A (655,359655{,}359 nodes) and B (22,129,15122{,}129{,}151 nodes) without a realisation; Without the symmetry reduction the two non-realisable searches, which exhaust the space, visit exactly twice as many nodes (1 310 7181\,310\,718 and 44 258 30244\,258\,302), since the global flip pairs off branches; the realisable case C is not doubled, because the search returns at the first witness found and may find it on either side of the pairing. The released script reports the doubled figure as an expectation for the exhausted cases and recomputes both on request (--full). ∎

The parity obstruction is released as q6_parity_obstruction.py (rank, coset weight enumeration and the three targets; standard library only, under a second), and the exhaustive decision as q6_decide_realizability.py (also standard library only, about twenty seconds). Its correctness is anchored at both ends: the reduction is checked against the released witness (recomputing mm from the spins in q6_odd_square_132.json gives {1:6,2:24,3:2}\{1{:}6,2{:}24,3{:}2\}, i.e. C), and the C branch of the search reconstructs a full spin vector whose recomputed hh-histogram and edge count are {0:2,2:24,4:6}\{0{:}2,2{:}24,4{:}6\} and 132132. Proposition 14 thus closes the question DPTV79 left open in 1979 and upgrades MPR95’s tentative “seems not to” to a proof – for both of the non-realisable distributions, where MPR95 spoke of one (DPTV79’s own sentence is plural: “We do not know if the other solutions given in table 1 for d=6d=6 are realizable”, p. 622). We stress that the mathematical content of the proposition — of the three optimal distributions, exactly one is realisable on a fixed side — stands independently of any reading of DPTV79’s Table I: that reading (obtained, as disclosed in Section 6, from the surrounding prose and the completeness of our own enumeration rather than from a direct transcription) enters only the historical identification of which question is thereby closed, not the proposition itself.

Earlier revisions of this manuscript reported instead a heuristic search (simulated annealing on the L1L_{1} distance between the current and target hh-histograms; 40 seeds for A and 20 for B at 300,000300{,}000 iterations each, all plateauing at distance 1616 and 88 respectively, against a positive control reaching C in 20/2020/20 runs at 60,00060{,}000 iterations). What the release contains is not the original runs: the bundled q6_other_distributions.py and its CSV/JSON are a re-execution of the same kind of search under a seed protocol newly specified for this package, as the provenance_note in both summary files states. They reproduce the numbers earlier revisions reported but are not the historical logs, which were not archived. They are in any case superseded by Proposition 14 and are no longer offered as evidence: a plateau is not a proof, and the asymmetry in iteration budget between the targets and the control makes the phrase “the same search” inexact. The two computations also range over different spaces: the annealing objective allows intermediate configurations with negative local fields (the archived logs record best-histogram entries at h=−4h=-4), whereas the reduction of Proposition 14 works with the nonnegative field 6−2​m​(v)6-2m(v) throughout. They agree on A and B, but they are not the same computation restricted.

Q7Q_{7}, g⁡(7)=304g(7)=304. The 304-edge odd-square value coincides with our originally announced Q7Q_{7} lower bound (Corollary 2); of the 19 86619\,866 solutions obtained via the SA-seed-plus-collector pipeline (Section 4), 389 are themselves odd-square witnesses of g⁡(7)=304g(7)=304 (Section 7), independently confirming reachability of this value without reference to [5].

Q8Q_{8}, g⁡(8)=682g(8)=682. We obtained a 682-edge odd-square witness for Q8Q_{8} from an explicit 256256-bit spin configuration together with the canonical fully frustrated coupling J⁡(x,dim)=(−1)popcount⁡(x&(2dim−1))J(x,\mathrm{dim})=(-1)^{\mathrm{popcount}(x\,\&\,(2^{\mathrm{dim}}-1))} (the coupling MPR95 write explicitly as their Eq. 4; one coupling convention realising a fully frustrated signature; see Section 6 supplementary script generate_q8_682.py). The script is dependency-free (Python standard library only), recomputes the edge set from the spin configuration, and asserts every structural quantity below against the recomputed data before writing the certificate; it does not take any of these quantities as input. Provenance of the spin configuration. The 256-bit configuration was derived by the author on 17–18 August 2026, using the canonical fully frustrated coupling of Marinari, Parisi, and Ritort [15], as recorded in dated correspondence with S. Lai, who independently reconstructed the identical 682-edge set from the shared spin vector and cross-checked all 1,792 squares, the degree distribution, and the local-field distribution before this material was incorporated into the manuscript. This provenance record is a first-person, dated account (the correspondence itself), not an independently reproducible computational log: no search seed, intermediate search records, or derivation script for the spin configuration itself is included in the released materials, only the scripts that regenerate and verify the edge set from the given spin configuration (Section 6). We do not claim this configuration is identical to any specific configuration MPR may have used internally, since they did not publish one; it is an independently derived witness attaining the same bound.

Reproducibility and the second witness. That leaves an asymmetry, and it should be stated with the two files kept apart: the headline certificate, q8_odd_square_682.json, remains the one released artefact whose derivation cannot be re-executed, and this revision does not close that provenance gap. What it does close is the reproducibility of the existence claim, through a second, independently regenerable 682682-edge witness: q8_A_recover.py is a fixed-seed search that finds, with no input from the released witness, a spin configuration realising the same optimal field distribution (seed 9000890008, hit at iteration 207 579207\,579 at the script’s default iteration budget: the budget parameter enters the annealing temperature schedule, so this exact hit – and the byte-identical output, which reproduce_core.py now asserts by SHA-256 – is conditional on the default 250 000250\,000-iteration setting, a different budget yielding a different, equally valid witness, and is scoped to the reference platform class: the acceptance step evaluates a floating-point exponential, so the byte-identity is an observed stability of CPython on IEEE-754 hardware with a standard libm (reproduced in our CPython 3.12 environment and, via an RNG-faithful independent re-implementation, by a reviewer), not a universal cross-platform guarantee — and it concerns only the byte-level identity of the regenerated file: the existence of a 682682-edge odd-square subgraph is carried platform-independently by the released static certificate and its dependency-free verification; 682682 edges, h|U={0:1,2:84,4:43}h|_{U}=\{0{:}1,2{:}84,4{:}43\}, square histogram {1:301,3:1491}\{1{:}301,3{:}1491\}, released as q8_A_witness.json). It is a different edge set from q8_odd_square_682.json, as expected. So the division of labour is: the existence of a 682682-edge odd-square subgraph is end-to-end reproducible via q8_A_witness.json, while the headline artefact q8_odd_square_682.json keeps its dated-correspondence provenance and is vouched for by verification, not by regeneration.

Proposition 15.

The witness edge set of q8_odd_square_682.json satisfies:

  1. (i)

    682682 edges, spanning all 256256 vertices of Q8Q_{8}.

  2. (ii)

    Square-intersection histogram {:301,:1491}\{1\!:\!301,\;3\!:\!1491\} over all 1 7921\,792 squares (odd-square condition holds everywhere; zero squares meet the edge set in 00, 22, or 44 edges).

  3. (iii)

    Degree sequence {42, 5168, 686}\{4^{2},\,5^{168},\,6^{86}\}; degree sum 1364=2⋅6821364=2\cdot 682.

  4. (iv)

    Local-field histogram {:2,:168,:86}\{0\!:\!2,\,2\!:\!168,\,4\!:\!86\} over all 256256 vertices, where the local field at a vertex is (positive degree) −- (negative degree) under the signed-graph correspondence above; restricted to UU specifically (the 128128 vertices summed over in Lemma 9 and the upper-bound derivation of Section 6.2), the histogram is {:1,:84,:43}\{0\!:\!1,\,2\!:\!84,\,4\!:\!43\}, giving ∑v∈Uh⁡(v)=2⋅84+4⋅43=340\sum_{v\in U}h(v)=2\cdot 84+4\cdot 43=340 directly.

  5. (v)

    Local maximality: every one of the 342342 non-edges of Q8Q_{8} creates at least 33 new C4C_{4}s upon addition (distribution {:41,:159,:120,:22}\{3\!:\!41,\,4\!:\!159,\,5\!:\!120,\,6\!:\!22\}), a strictly stronger local-maximality margin than the originally announced 680-edge Solution B of Section 5, for which 2 of 344 non-edges created only 1 or 2 new C4C_{4}s.

All quantities in Proposition 15 were recomputed independently of the reconstruction script by direct enumeration of all 1 7921\,792 squares against the released edge list, using the strict definition of C4C_{4}-freeness from Lemma 3 (no square may have all four edges present); this independent check found zero violations and is fully reproducible from the released files alone. The reconstruction, its SHA-256 checksum, and an independent audit are additionally reported to have been cross-checked against S. Lai’s separately produced implementation, with full agreement; this cross-check is recorded as a dated correspondence account (as in Section 6.3), not as an independently verifiable artefact, since the correspondence, Lai’s implementation, and its output are not included in the released materials. The regenerable second witness q8_A_witness.json (seed 9000890008; Section 6.3) shares items (i)–(iii) and the full and UU-restricted histograms of item (iv) verbatim; its local-maximality margin distribution is {3:42, 4:151, 5:133, 6:16}\{3{:}42,\,4{:}151,\,5{:}133,\,6{:}16\} over the same 342342 non-edges. These were recomputed here by the same direct square enumeration; in addition, verify.py now checks both 682682-edge certificates (odd-square condition, edge count, and the respective margin distributions), and reproduce_core.py asserts the second witness’s byte-level regeneration by SHA-256.

Second n=8n=8 witness. The local-field distribution {0:1,2:84,4:43}\{0{:}1,2{:}84,4{:}43\} above is one of two optimal field distributions for n=8n=8 returned by the exhaustive integer programme solve_field_ip.py. The other, {2:87,4:40,6:1}\{2{:}87,4{:}40,6{:}1\}, is realised by additional witnesses found by the same canonical fully frustrated coupling together with a targeted simulated annealing whose objective is the L1L_{1} distance between the current hh-histogram on UU and the target {2:87,4:40,6:1}\{2{:}87,4{:}40,6{:}1\}. Over 2020 seeds ×\times 300,000300{,}000 iterations, 22 runs reached the target (L1=0L_{1}=0) at seeds 2026120720261207 (iteration 260,621260{,}621) and 2026121820261218 (iteration 276,842276{,}842); these seed values are arbitrary RNG integers and are not dates, despite their form. To confirm that nothing depends on that choice, the same search re-run from the unrelated base 9020090200 also reaches the target (seed 9021090210, iteration 279 646279\,646). The remaining 1717 stopped at L1=6L_{1}=6 and 11 at L1=8L_{1}=8. Failed intermediate states can contain negative local fields (for example h=−6h=-6 in one recorded run), because the annealing objective explores non-maximal configurations; Lemma 11 applies only to a maximum odd-square edge set and is not contradicted by such intermediates. Both witnesses are released in q8_B_witnesses.json (spins and edges), regenerable via q8_B_recover.py, and verified by the dependency-free verify_q8_B_witnesses.py. The two successful runs can be checked directly from the stored certificates without any search; the other eighteen are recorded only by their plateau distances, so confirming those requires rerunning the protocol, which q8_B_recover.py supports (it is seeded per trial and takes --seeds and --iters). The 20-run success/plateau tally is provenance information rather than part of the theorem’s evidence and is not rerun by the default one-command reproduction. Nothing in the claim depends on it — the assertion is existence, and two certificates carry it:

Proposition 16.

Each witness in q8_B_witnesses.json satisfies:

  1. (i)

    682682 edges, all valid Q8Q_{8} edges, no repetitions.

  2. (ii)

    Square histogram {1:301, 3:1491}\{1{:}301,\,3{:}1491\} over all 1,7921{,}792 squares (odd-square; C4C_{4}-free).

  3. (iii)

    hh-histogram {2:87, 4:40, 6:1}\{2{:}87,\,4{:}40,\,6{:}1\} on UU, ∑h=340\sum h=340, ∑h2=1024\sum h^{2}=1024 (✓). On the opposite side UcU^{c} the histogram is {0:1,2:84,4:43}\{0{:}1,2{:}84,4{:}43\}, i.e. the other optimal n=8n=8 field distribution. Thus each of these single edge sets realises the two optimal histograms on its two bipartition classes.

  4. (iv)

    Local maximality with margin at least 33. For the witnesses with seeds 2026120720261207 and 2026121820261218, respectively, the non-edge violation distributions are

    {3:34,4:169,5:121,6:18}and{3:41,4:154,5:130,6:17}.\{3{:}34,4{:}169,5{:}121,6{:}18\}\quad\text{and}\quad\{3{:}41,4{:}154,5{:}130,6{:}17\}.

Thus n=8n=8 differs from n=6n=6: every optimal field distribution for n=8n=8 is realisable by an explicit odd-square 682682-edge subgraph of Q8Q_{8}, while for n=6n=6 only distribution C is (Proposition 14). The two halves of that contrast rest on different kinds of evidence, and the asymmetry should be stated: at n=8n=8 both realisations are exhibited constructively, whereas at n=6n=6 non-realisability is proved exhaustively. Thus “every optimal distribution is realisable” at n=8n=8 means constructive existence for each of the two DP distributions, not an exhaustive decision over all n=8n=8 spin assignments of the kind performed at n=6n=6. We have not attempted the analogous decision at n=8n=8. The obstacle is not the raw size of the space — the reduction gives 21272^{127} after pinning one spin, and at n=6n=6 a 2322^{32} space was settled in between 501501 and 2.2×1072.2\times 10^{7} nodes — but that the counter-overflow pruning which makes the n=6n=6 search collapse has no guarantee of biting as hard at n=8n=8. The parity obstruction, however, transfers and explains part of the contrast: the rank of the U×UcU\times U^{c} map over GF⁡(2)\mathrm{GF}(2) is 1,4,4,16,16,64,64,2561,4,4,16,16,64,64,256 for n=2,…,9n=2,\ldots,9 (the full sequence is recomputed and asserted by q6_parity_obstruction.py, which runs in the default reproducibility path), so it is full exactly when nn is odd. There is thus no parity obstruction at all at n=7n=7, and one at both n=6n=6 and n=8n=8; at n=8n=8 the criterion reads k⁡(v)k(v) odd ⇔h⁡(v)∈{2,6}\iff h(v)\in\{2,6\}, so the two optimal distributions require weights 8888 and 8484, and the released witnesses show both are attained. This is a second axis, independent of the field identity, along which n=7n=7 differs from its even neighbours.
